dossier_refresh.thesis_summary: Wave Life Sciences holds an FDA-GRANTED, not-yet-held meeting to discuss a potential accelerated-approval pathway for WVE-006 (GalNAc RNA editing) in alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency. Verified verbatim in the 30 July 2026 Q2 release: the meeting request "was granted by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA)" and "is scheduled for the end of summer 2026." The event is real, idiosyncratic (resolves on Wave's own AAT biomarker package and FDA judgement, not the tape), and UNFIRED as of 4 August 2026 - but it has slipped a full quarter (Wave's 18 May 2026 release guided "regulatory feedback ... mid-2026"), it is season-dated rather than calendar-dated, it is non-binding (minutes and guidance, no decision, no payout), and minutes customarily arrive ~30 days post-meeting, pointing disclosure into the company's own "investor day in the fall of 2026." The load-bearing asymmetry is not probability but PAYOFF: Beam Therapeutics already secured FDA alignment on a biomarker-based accelerated pathway for BEAM-302 in the same indication on 25 March 2026 (12-month AAT biomarker endpoint, 60 mg dose), so a favourable Wave answer is confirmation of an established agency precedent, not a revelation. dossier_refresh.kill_risk: The most load-bearing claim in the thesis is that a favourable FDA answer pays. It may not. Three live facts push against it. (1) PRECEDENT ALREADY SET: Beam obtained FDA alignment on an AAT-biomarker accelerated pathway for BEAM-302 on 25 March 2026, so "FDA open to biomarker AA in AATD" is priced knowledge; Wave winning re-rates the company only to the extent its own levels look competitive. (2) THEY DO NOT: on Wave's own 18 May 2026 numbers, functional wild-type M-AAT is 11.9 uM x 64.4% = 7.7 uM (200 mg biweekly) and 13.6 uM x 58.7% = 8.0 uM (400 mg monthly) - both BELOW the ~11 uM augmentation-therapy protective threshold, versus Beam's 16.1 uM total at 94% M-AAT = ~15.1 uM functional. The agency can grant the endpoint class and still require a dose/level Wave has not yet shown, which converts a "win" into a reset timeline pending the 600 mg monthly cohort. (3) NO CLEAN DISCLOSURE EVENT: minutes are private, ~30 days post-meeting, and the company's stated venue is a fall investor day - Wave controls both the timing and the framing, so the "resolution" can arrive as a bundled narrative slide rather than a printable answer. Residual: the position can be right on the science and still collect no repricing.

(3) The floor is not static: at roughly $40M/quarter burn, net cash falls from ~$2.50/sh today to ~$1.50-1.70/sh by the early-2027 C-FORWARD readout, and a pre-approval financing inside that window is plausible, so the "cash floor" is both decaying and dilutable. (4) Regime check: XBI at a 5-year high means this name failed to rally on the best result it could realistically produce in the most receptive biotech tape in five years — the most parsimonious reading is that the market has priced the commercial opportunity correctly at near zero, not that a deep, attentive, event-focused register misjudged a result it had waited eighteen months for.

WHY ONLY ONE. With no head-count cap, dilution is the entire cost model, and the honest test is binary: is this name at least as good as the median seat already held? Two structural findings did most of the work. First, the FAST-RETURN rule: five of eleven survivors (NAMS, CMCSA, LBTYK, IFF, and effectively IMTX on its undated event-count drift) resolve in 2027 or later, so they are passes on the mandate regardless of how wide their spreads look. Second — and this is the finding worth carrying forward — seven of eleven survivors are valuation_method=binary_prob, and FIVE of those seven have no usable defined-risk expression at all: ALVO has no listed chain whatsoever, SVRA's November monthly expires two days BEFORE its PDUFA, VNDA's true +1 monthly (Mar-2027) is completely untraded, and IMMX/IMTX carry 5 and 19 contracts of interest respectively. Under the hard gate that binaries must be defined-risk only, a correct thesis in a contract with no two-sided quote is not a trade. Expression is my only risk lever now that sizing is gone, and on this batch the lever simply was not available.

AGIO IS THE EXCEPTION AND IT EARNS THE DILUTION. It is the only clean TRADE with no conditions, the only name with a payoff ratio above 1 (1.62:1), the only one whose dossier was struck on today's tape with zero compression, and the only binary here with a chain that satisfies the gate with margin — Dec-18 is a full +1 monthly past the first clearing expiry, so a delayed action letter does not kill the structure. I carry the CRO's caveat that the option leg is capacity-limited (572 calls/day) and must be worked with limits at the mid — at a 5% paper seat that is a workable constraint, not a disqualifier.

DEBT-CYCLE JUDGEMENT (advisory, not a gate). DISCIPLINE punishes the cost of waiting, and this batch splits cleanly along that line without my having to use the phase as a filter. AGIO is exactly the shape that gets paid in this phase: an approval that turns into launch revenue on top of a franchise already run-rating ~$179M and growing 3.6x, with a floor built from net cash plus an APPROVED product rather than from a story. The three sum-of-parts names — CMCSA, LBTYK, IFF — are the opposite shape: distant terminal-value re-rates into mid-2027 fighting a real 30y at 2.98% and rising, two of them on eroding or unverifiable asset bases. I am passing all three on the 2026 horizon rule; the phase corroborates that call but is not what makes it. Note also that the DISCIPLINE read on financing-contingent milestones is live in this batch — LBTYK's cash bridge needs ~$1.5bn of unexecuted H2 disposals whose proceeds the company has earmarked for SUBSIDIARY debt, and ALVO answered a CRL with a $165M raise followed two weeks later by a $75M term loan.
